subject.title: fix(agents): use fetchWithSsrFGuard in minimax-vlm.ts instead of raw fetch

question: Should a configured MiniMax VLM base URL implicitly authorize private-network access, or must private access require the existing explicit SSRF policy?
rationale: The current patch preserves legacy private endpoints by trusting every custom origin, while existing security patterns avoid deriving private-network authorization solely from a configured URL; choosing the intended compatibility boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Require Explicit Private Access
options.body: Thread the existing SSRF policy into MiniMax VLM and keep private-network access disabled unless operators explicitly enable it.

options.title: Preserve Safe Private Origins
options.body: Keep implicit configured-origin compatibility but reject metadata-like hosts, link-local addresses, and known cloud metadata IPs as the provider transport does.

options.title: Pause Guarded-Fetch Migration
options.body: Leave the raw-fetch path unchanged until the private-endpoint compatibility contract is documented and tested.

recommendation.title: Require Explicit Private Access
recommendation.body: Thread the existing SSRF policy into MiniMax VLM and keep private-network access disabled unless operators explicitly enable it.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent provider transport and image-fetch security work most directly defines the relevant configured-origin boundary.
